purpose: Measure read-only, multi-hop code-navigation outcomes and observed BB event timelines before changing plugin behavior. This is not a raw-search-engine or CPU benchmark.

tasks.prompt: Read-only task. In the Go repository, where is the package-level Decode function defined? Name the constructor it uses and the Decode method it ultimately calls. Answer in two short bullets: file path; then the delegation chain. Do not edit files.

Read-only task. In the Rust repository, trace anyhow::Error::new from its definition to the constructor which builds Error { inner }. Answer in two short bullets: file path; then the complete chain, including the intermediate function and final constructor. Do not edit files.
Read-only task. In the C repository, where is cJSON_Parse defined and which parser function does it delegate to? Answer in two short bullets: file path; then the delegation. Do not edit files.

Read-only task. In the C++ repository, trace the locale-taking fmt::format overload to the lower-level function that writes into its buffer. Answer in two short bullets: file path; then the complete call chain including the intermediate formatter and buffer call. Do not edit files.

Read-only task. In the Java repository, trace Gson.fromJson(String, Class) through its TypeToken conversion and StringReader overload to the adapter read. Answer in two short bullets: file path; then the complete chain including the TypeToken operation, reader creation, adapter lookup, and read call. Do not edit files.

threadRules: Use a fresh thread for every repetition.
Use the same provider, model, reasoning level, permission mode, fixture workspace, and exact prompt in every arm.
Do not tell the agent which search tool to prefer.
For plugin arms, record the configured instruction style with --instruction-style and keep the plugin commit fixed.
protocol.successRule: A response is correct only when it includes the expected path substring and every required term, evaluated against the final visible answer.
protocol.timingRule: Event-timeline durations are reported only when the selected completed turn has complete, non-ambiguous lifecycle pairs. They are observed intervals, not CPU time, hidden-reasoning duration, or causal proof.
protocol.interpretation: Compare correctness first, then completed discovery operations and shell fallbacks. Treat timeline fields as diagnostics for selecting one plugin-only optimization, not as a general performance claim.
